title: Test and evaluate my model
subject: Design & Technology
label: Public edition
objective_verbatim: CONSTRUCTION: test and evaluate what I made.
assessment_verbatim: F: safe-working observation.  S: constructed product + evaluation (data drop).

sources.note: Current main bytes match the accepted unchanged source; workbook not redistributed.
W3 16–20 Nov; W4 23–27 Nov. One lesson weekly per line; no day or slot inferred.

external_sources.title: HSE: Health and safety checklist for classrooms
external_sources.supports: The ordinary classroom checklist excludes specialist D&T; staff use activity-appropriate risk controls and local procedures.

external_sources.title: Science Buddies: Build the Best Paper Bridge
external_sources.supports: Folding a sheet into a channel can change how it resists bending. The local dimensions, light block test and stop rules are authored classroom choices; no strength result is assumed.

evidence.description: An actual test record for up to three identical light blocks, including stop/not-tried entries, observed results and a justified proposed improvement.
evidence.status: contribution to source assessment; no completion claim

routes.Supported: Supported: place one block with help.
routes.Independent: Independent: test, observe and record each step.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: explain how to make a comparison fair.

vocab.definition: A planned check of how something works.
Look closely and notice what happens.
Use results to judge how well it worked.
Make a change that aims to help.
Using the same conditions for comparison.

cases.text: Check the model, tray and equal-height supports. Set a 10 cm gap.
cases.fact: A stable setup makes the check meaningful.
cases.next_step: Ask staff to approve the setup before loading.
cases.staff_note: If the model or supports are damaged/unstable, do not test. Record not tested and the reason.

cases.text: Use the same set of three identical light blocks.
cases.next_step: Keep the agreed block type, gap and centre position.
cases.staff_note: Staff select large light foam or plastic blocks and trial the setup. No coins, heavy masses or small choking-risk items.

cases.text: Put one block at the centre. Wait five seconds.
cases.fact: The first check uses one block.
cases.next_step: Look from the side; record what you see.
cases.staff_note: Hands stay clear during the observation. No touching underneath to support the bridge.

cases.text: If stable, try two blocks, then three. Check for five seconds each time.
cases.fact: Each load is checked before adding more.
cases.next_step: Use the same central loading place and stop at three.
cases.staff_note: If blocks cannot be stacked safely in the centre, stop and adapt under staff control. Do not continue just to complete a table.

cases.text: Stop if the model slips, splits or bends sharply. Tell the adult.
cases.fact: The model or load is becoming unstable.
cases.next_step: Let the adult remove the blocks. Record the result.
cases.staff_note: A slight bend can be recorded; a sharp bend, split or slip ends the test. Do not load to destruction.

cases.text: Use one result to suggest an improvement.
cases.fact: A claim should match what was observed.
cases.next_step: Say what happened, what to change and why.
cases.staff_note: “Held three” means it held the highest load tried here, not its maximum possible strength. A change is proposed, not claimed effective without a later fair retest.

Purpose and success checks
What does a fair test tell me about my model?
I can follow a safe test plan. I can record what I actually observe. I can use a result to suggest an improvement.
LAUNCH-DT-W4-E1: An actual test record for up to three identical light blocks, including stop/not-tried entries, observed results and a justified proposed improvement.
Before pupils arrive

Retrieve each Week 3 model and work reference. Staff trial a stable setup with equal-height supports, a 10 cm gap and a tray. Select three identical large light foam/plastic blocks that can sit safely at the centre; set a lower cap if local risk controls require. Have rulers, a five-second timer and evidence sheets. Provide a model for a missed build, clearly labelled staff-made.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.

Access and practice
Supported: place one block with help. Independent: test, observe and record each step. Aspire: explain how to make a comparison fair.

Demonstrate on a separate example. Pupils test their own model with support, one load at a time up to three blocks. Record observations as they happen. If a staff-made substitute is used, mark whose model it is. The learner can still evidence testing, but not claim the earlier building work.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

Staff approve and supervise each setup. Use a stable low desk/tray; keep hands clear of the loaded model. No body-weight tests, heavy loads or deliberate collapse. Stop for slipping, splitting or sharp bending; adult removes the blocks. If conditions are unsuitable, record not tested and evaluate the setup instead. No invented result for an absent or stopped test.
Assessment and feedback

Record actual block counts and observations at each attempted load. Leave later loads as not tried after a stop. Controls: same model, 10 cm support gap, block type, central loading and five-second observation. An evaluation links a real observation to a reasoned change, for example neater folds or a secure agreed join. Three blocks is a classroom cap, not a strength rating. No result is prefilled.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school's evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Speaking listening and writing

Give a clear observation, listen to the stop instruction and explain an improvement using a result. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Model and hinge

Check the model and the 10 cm gap. Put one light block at the centre. Wait five seconds and look from the side. If stable, try two, then three blocks. Stop if it slips, splits or bends sharply. Record what happened. Use it to suggest a change.

B. Stop the test and let the adult remove the load safely. Record the slip as an observation. A ignores the stop rule; C changes the test and conceals the result. Re-model the stop signal with an empty setup, not by deliberately breaking a model.
Individual evidence key

Record actual block counts and observations at each attempted load. Leave later loads as not tried after a stop. Controls: same model, 10 cm support gap, block type, central loading and five-second observation. An evaluation links a real observation to a reasoned change, for example neater folds or a secure agreed join. Three blocks is a classroom cap, not a strength rating. No result is prefilled.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: If the model or supports are damaged/unstable, do not test. Record not tested and the reason.
Card B: Staff select large light foam or plastic blocks and trial the setup. No coins, heavy masses or small choking-risk items.
Card C: Hands stay clear during the observation. No touching underneath to support the bridge.
Card D: If blocks cannot be stacked safely in the centre, stop and adapt under staff control. Do not continue just to complete a table.
Card E: A slight bend can be recorded; a sharp bend, split or slip ends the test. Do not load to destruction.
Card F: “Held three” means it held the highest load tried here, not its maximum possible strength. A change is proposed, not claimed effective without a later fair retest.
Common misunderstandings

Not tried is different from failed. Holding three blocks does not prove three is the maximum load. Holding the model with a hand changes the test. A proposed improvement is not proven until checked under comparable conditions. An unsuccessful model can still provide useful evidence.
Teaching boundary

Staff approve and supervise each setup. Use a stable low desk/tray; keep hands clear of the loaded model. No body-weight tests, heavy loads or deliberate collapse. Stop for slipping, splitting or sharp bending; adult removes the blocks. If conditions are unsuitable, record not tested and evaluate the setup instead. No invented result for an absent or stopped test.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
